fact_text: The Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana loans were described in the programme as carrying a 5 percent interest rate.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: An earlier subsidised housing loan scheme offered 5 percent loans of up to Rs 5 million, according to the interviewee, who said it was launched by the previous government.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: The chairman of a builders and developers association, Abad Hassan Bakhshi, called the Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana scheme a non-starter because its loan size is too small for a home in a Pakistani city.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: The interviewee said the State Bank did not market the scheme well, and that builders do not push it because the loan amount is too small to help their customers buy homes.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: The interviewee put construction cost in most of Pakistan at about Rs 6,000 per square foot, moving by about Rs 1,500 between Tier 1, Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: The interviewee said he knows of no legal construction in Pakistan below Rs 7,000 per square foot, so a 1,000 sq ft flat would cost about Rs 70 lakh before land.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: The interviewee argued the scheme loan would need to rise from about Rs 2 million to roughly Rs 10 million before ordinary buyers could use it to build a legal home.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: At Rs 6,000 per sq ft, a Rs 2 million loan at 5 percent would buy about 300 sq ft of construction, before land and approval costs.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: Building approvals add further cost, which the interviewee said agencies collect both as official fees and under the table; his cost estimate excludes these charges.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: Documentation for a Rs 2 million home loan costs about Rs 1.5 to 2 lakh, the interviewee said, which he argued makes the loan unattractive to buyers.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: A 1,000 sq ft regulated flat with four rooms would cost at least Rs 80 to 85 lakh, and a 500 sq ft flat about Rs 40 to 45 lakh, according to the interviewee.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: The interviewee said a family needs a flat of about 800 to 1,000 sq ft for light, air, sleep and space, so affordability should not be solved by shrinking the unit.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: The interviewee said a typical Karachi household pays about Rs 35,000 a month in rent, and proposed setting loan instalments close to that rent level.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: The interviewee said earlier housing loans have 99 percent recovery, with 1 percent defaulted non-performing loans, against about 4 percent default on car loans.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: The interviewee estimated Pakistan's housing shortfall at about 14 million homes, up from 12 million in an earlier World Bank estimate he cited.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: Karachi Building Control Authority approvals for public-sale projects fell from about 500 a year to about 5 to 7 a month, the interviewee said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: Cement, steel, wire and tile makers are running at about 40 to 50 percent of production, the interviewee said, as new projects stall.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: The interviewee said property transfer costs in Pakistan are very high, higher than in the rest of the region, which discourages formal buying and selling.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: The interviewee blamed inconsistent policy, high taxes, unsecured land titles and informal two-number documents for holding back developers and buyers in Pakistan's housing market.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: The interviewee argued a revived construction sector could generate about Rs 1 trillion in tax revenue, so supporting housing finance would pay back the state.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: The interviewee said illegal construction in Karachi is about 10 times the volume of legal construction, driven by buyers who cannot afford regulated housing.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: Middle-income earners struggle to save for a home after paying school fees, food, rent and medical bills, so many rent instead, the interviewee said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: Ordinary buyers, the interviewee said, must raise a deposit by selling family gold, inheriting property or borrowing from friends and relatives.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: The interviewee argued that officials deciding housing policy from air-conditioned offices lack a sense of public needs, which he said explains why most housing schemes fail.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)

fact_text: The interviewee said informal settlements in Sri Lanka and India were turned into regulated housing schemes, a route he said Pakistan has not taken because policy is inconsistent.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Mera Ghar Mera Ashiana: What Went Wrong? | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-08)
